newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EDGE HIGHER ON TUESDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EDGE HIGHER ON TUESDAY.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted firmer on Tuesday, dealers said.
The central Reserve Bank offered Z$500 million worth of treasury bills but only Z$248 million worth were taken up at 20.99 percent, up from 19.43 percent at Monday's auction.
NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 20.75 percent from 20.5 percent and sold at around 20 percent.

Bankers acceptances, which were quoted at 20 percent (buying) the previous day, were being bought and sold on Tuesday at 20.99 and 20.1 percent respectively. Call money however shed one percentage point to 17 percent.
The Reserve Bank said the market closed on Monday with a Z$133.9 million shortage compared to a surplus of Z$43 million for Saturday.
